name: inbox-manager
description: Classify, prioritize, summarize, and draft responses for inbound messages without sending or modifying external communications.
inputs: Approved message text or message summaries.
Known sender, channel, date, and context, when available.
Business priorities, routing rules, or triage categories.
Tone guidance or response constraints, when approved.
Applicable approval policy for outbound communication.
outputs: Draft response or response options, when useful.
Open questions, missing context, and approval needs.

name: meeting-notes
description: Convert transcripts or meeting notes into concise summaries, confirmed decisions, action items, and follow-ups.
inputs: Transcript, rough notes, or meeting recording-derived text.
Meeting date, attendees, topic, and purpose, when available.
Known project or business context.
Preferred action-item owner and due-date format, if specified.
outputs: Action items with owners and due dates when stated.
Unresolved topics and inferred items clearly labeled.

name: competitor-analysis
description: Compare competitors from evidence while distinguishing confirmed facts, inference, and uncertainty.
inputs: Competitor names, market category, geography, and comparison goal.
Approved source materials, links, notes, or research outputs.
Comparison criteria such as offer, pricing, positioning, audience, channels, or proof.
Freshness requirements and known constraints.

name: marketing-monday
description: Produce a recurring marketing brief that summarizes performance, customer or audience signals, priorities, and recommended next steps.
inputs: Approved campaign, content, audience, sales, or customer signal data.
Reporting period and business priorities.
Known experiments, launches, offers, or market events.
Performance metrics and source notes, when available.
Requested brief format or audience.
outputs: Open questions, risks, and follow-up analysis needs.

name: reputation-review
description: Analyze reviews, comments, or customer feedback, group themes, and draft response options without publishing them.
inputs: Approved reviews, comments, testimonials, complaints, or feedback excerpts.
Source, date, rating, product, service, or channel context, when available.
Response tone guidance and escalation rules.
Known business facts relevant to the feedback.
Applicable approval policy for public or private responses.

name: report-builder
description: Combine approved internal data into a concise operational report for review, coordination, or decision support.
inputs: Approved internal data, notes, metrics, or status updates.
Reporting period, audience, and decision context.
Required sections, format, or level of detail.
Known risks, blockers, approvals, and unresolved questions.
outputs: Risks, blockers, dependencies, and open questions.

name: sop-builder
description: Convert a repeated process into a clear standard operating procedure while preserving human approval points and safety boundaries.
inputs: Process description, observed steps, notes, or existing checklist.
Process owner, audience, trigger, and desired outcome.
Required tools, inputs, outputs, and constraints.
Known approval points, safety boundaries, exceptions, and escalation rules.
outputs: Roles, triggers, steps, checks, and expected outputs.
Exceptions, safety boundaries, and unresolved questions.

name: follow-up
description: Prepare follow-up context, draft sequences, and next-step recommendations while preserving tone, sales intent, and approval boundaries.
inputs: Approved sales context, prior conversation notes, or lead history.
Desired outcome, sales stage, and follow-up reason.
Tone guidance, cadence constraints, and channel preference.
Known objections, open questions, or promised next steps.
Applicable approval policy for outbound communication.
outputs: Suggested sequence or single follow-up draft.

name: proposal-builder
description: Combine approved business context and client requirements into a clear proposal draft without sending or making commercial commitments.
inputs: Approved business context, offer details, and constraints.
Client requirements, goals, pain points, and success criteria.
Pricing, scope, timeline, and terms only when approved.
Relevant prior discussions, research, or qualification notes.
Required proposal format or sections.

name: speed-to-lead
description: Identify, prioritize, and prepare rapid response drafts for new leads while preserving approval boundaries.
inputs: Approved lead details or inquiry text.
Source, timestamp, requested service or product, and contact context, when available.
Qualification criteria, response tone, and routing rules.
Existing customer or opportunity context, when approved.
Applicable approval policy for outbound communication.
outputs: Rapid response draft or response options.
Recommended next action and approval needs.

name: handoff
description: Convert completed work or session context into concise durable project state that another agent or future session can use without reading raw chat history.
inputs: Completed work summary.
Verified facts and evidence.
Changed files or affected areas.
Open tasks, blockers, and unresolved decisions.
Relevant assumptions or uncertainties.
Existing canonical project-state files, when present.
Explicit human approvals or confirmations relevant to the session.
outputs: The smallest sufficient set of updates to affected canonical project-state files.
A concise closeout report identifying updated files, untouched files, unresolved items, and validation status.
No project-state file changes when the session produced no durable state change.

name: knowledge-ingest
description: Integrate source material into the provider-neutral LLM Wiki while preserving raw evidence, provenance, uncertainty, and the boundary from operational project state.
inputs: Source material or a stable reference to it.
Known provenance, access constraints, and source limitations.
Requested ingest scope.
Existing knowledge index, source cards, and relevant wiki pages.
outputs: Preserved raw source location or stable source reference.
New or updated source card when needed.
Updated existing wiki pages, or a justified new page when no suitable page exists.
Updated knowledge index when page structure changes.
Concise INGEST record appended to the knowledge operation log.

name: knowledge-lint
description: Inspect the LLM Wiki for quality, consistency, provenance, navigation, duplication, and knowledge gaps without silently rewriting knowledge.
inputs: Requested lint scope.
`../../../shared/knowledge/index.md`.
Wiki pages, source cards, and raw references needed for the checks.
Canonical LINT checks and policy.
outputs: Concise LINT record appended to the knowledge operation log.

name: knowledge-query
description: Retrieve the minimum relevant long-term knowledge for a task while preserving provenance, uncertainty, and separation from current project state.
inputs: Question or task.
`../../../shared/knowledge/index.md`.
Relevant wiki pages selected from the index.
Source cards or raw material only when verification requires them.
outputs: Concise answer based on the minimum relevant knowledge.
Confirmed knowledge, inference, uncertainty, conflicts, and gaps kept distinguishable.
Recommendation for a later INGEST operation when durable new synthesis would improve the wiki.

name: project-audit
description: Inspect a project's current state, repository health, documentation, tests, blockers, and risks without modifying the target project by default.
inputs: Target project path or project identifier.
Audit objective.
Known constraints, protected areas, or read-only requirements.
Relevant project instructions or governance files.
Available deterministic checks.
outputs: Clear note of any checks not run.

name: research
description: Collect, verify, compare, and synthesize evidence so decisions can rely on traceable sources rather than unsupported assumptions.
inputs: Research question.
Decision context and constraints.
Preferred or required source types.
Known sources, documents, repositories, or links.
Freshness or jurisdiction requirements, if relevant.
outputs: Source list with enough detail for review.
Comparison of viable options, when relevant.
Concise synthesis and recommended next step, if requested.

name: review
description: Independently validate completed work for quality, safety, requirement coverage, and evidence before acceptance, escalation, or human approval.
inputs: User request or acceptance criteria.
Executor output.
Changed files, artifacts, or findings.
Runtime-observed mutation evidence for controlled-write executions, including scope violations and target fingerprints.
Tool results and validation evidence.
Known risks, constraints, and required approvals.
outputs: Required fixes, escalation reason, or approval question.

name: skill-creator
description: Design a new reusable, provider-neutral skill package that can be tested, reviewed, and adapted by future providers without changing its canonical intent.
inputs: Requested skill name.
Problem or recurring task the skill should address.
Expected users or agents.
Known constraints and risks.
Available deterministic tools, scripts, references, or examples.
outputs: Clear expected inputs and outputs for the skill.
Checks that can validate correct use.
Notes about provider-specific adaptation needs, if any.

name: caption-writer
description: Draft channel-appropriate caption options from supplied content, facts, tone, and objectives.
inputs: Content brief or source asset description.
Supplied channel context, audience, objective, tone, length, facts, and call to action.
Required terms, prohibited claims, and accessibility context.
outputs: Optional short, standard, or alternate-tone variants when requested.
Claim, source, accessibility, and review notes.

name: comment-analysis
description: Analyze supplied comments or community signals for recurring themes, questions, sentiment, risks, and response opportunities without replying publicly.
inputs: Approved comments, messages, or community-signal excerpts.
Supplied channel context, period, language, objective, and sampling notes.
Escalation rules and relevant verified business facts.
outputs: Theme groups, recurring questions, sentiment signals, and representative paraphrases.
Risk, urgency, moderation, product, or content opportunity notes.
Optional response themes or draft options when requested.

name: competitor-monitor
description: Analyze competitor social content patterns from approved evidence without turning channel observations into unsupported market-level conclusions.
inputs: Competitor set, supplied channel context, period, comparison goal, and criteria.
Approved posts, observations, exports, links, or research outputs with source dates.
Freshness requirements and known evidence gaps.
outputs: Confirmed observations, interpretations, uncertainty, and evidence gaps.
Internal opportunities, watch items, and follow-up research needs.

name: content-calendar
description: Create a channel-level content calendar that turns approved goals and source material into an internal publishing plan.
inputs: Planning period, supplied channel context, goals, audiences, themes, and available assets.
Cadence, format, timing, campaign, and capacity constraints.
Approved prior performance or community signals, when available.
outputs: Calendar entries with date or sequence, channel context, format, topic, objective, source asset, and draft status.
Coverage, dependency, uncertainty, and review notes.

name: content-repurpose
description: Transform approved source material into distinct channel-level social drafts while preserving meaning, attribution, and factual boundaries.
inputs: Approved source content and provenance.
Target channel or format contexts, audiences, objectives, tone, and length constraints.
Required calls to action, links, credits, and prohibited claims.
outputs: Separate draft variants for each supplied target context.
Source-to-draft traceability, adaptation notes, and missing-asset or review needs.

name: hook-generator
description: Generate opening ideas for supplied social content without overstating claims or inventing evidence.
inputs: Topic, content premise, audience, desired action, and supplied channel or format context.
Approved facts, proof, tone, constraints, and prohibited claims.
Requested number or range of hook styles.
outputs: Distinct hook drafts with optional style or use notes.

name: performance-review
description: Review supplied channel or content performance data and produce evidence-backed findings and next-test recommendations.
inputs: Content item or channel scope, reporting period, objective, and supplied metrics.
Metric definitions, comparison baseline, prior tests, and known data limitations.
Supplied channel or format context.
outputs: Performance summary tied to the stated objective.
Metric changes, possible explanations, uncertainty, and data-quality notes.

name: post-planner
description: Plan one channel-level social content item before copywriting, production, review, or publication.
inputs: Supplied channel and format context.
Objective, audience, topic, source material, call to action, and constraints.
Relevant approved performance or campaign context.
outputs: Post brief with objective, audience, core message, format, structure, asset needs, call to action, and success signal.
Assumptions, risks, dependencies, and review notes.

name: weekly-social-report
description: Create an internal weekly report that combines supplied content activity, channel performance, community signals, learnings, and next actions.
inputs: Reporting period, supplied channel context, objectives, content log, and metrics.
Performance-review, comment-analysis, and competitor-monitor findings when available.
Prior-period baseline, experiments, constraints, and known data gaps.
outputs: Content, community, competitor, learning, risk, and next-action sections.
Data-quality, uncertainty, ownership, and approval notes.
